subject: Proposed MSA redlines — service sunsetting / notice & wind-down timing
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@datumops.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@datumops.com
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MSA redlines — notice windows + wind-down

Jordan — attaching our third pass on the MSA (DatumOps_MSA_Redlines_v3.pdf) and an updated order form. We want to be explicit about two things: (1) the auto-renew mechanics and how "opt-out" happens for pilot/term contracts, and (2) a clear wind-down/transition assistance commitment in the event of termination for convenience.

High-level asks from DatumOps:
- Auto-renew: prefer auto-renew only if both parties confirm in writing 30 days prior to the renewal date; otherwise the contract should not auto-renew.
- Termination for convenience: allow DatumOps or Redwood to terminate with 60 days' notice; require a 45-day transition assistance period where Redwood provides export and engineering support (SLA defined in Order Form).
- Pro-rated credit: if Redwood terminates for convenience, DatumOps requests a pro-rated credit for unused pre-paid capacity (standard).

Can you confirm whether these are acceptable? If anything on our redlines is a hard stop, call it out and we can escalate. We aim to get to final redlines by 10 Sep.

Attachments: DatumOps_MSA_Redlines_v3.pdf (pdf, 78KB), OrderForm_DatumOps_20260901.docx (docx, 55KB)

Best,

Samir — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Looping in Priyom (AE) and Laura (legal) to weigh in. A couple quick clarifying questions from my side:

1) On auto-renew: do you mean no mechanical auto-renew unless Redwood gets affirmative written confirmation from DatumOps 30 days before the renewal date? That deviates from our standard (auto-renew unless Customer opts out 60 days prior) so we need to be clear about the timeline.

2) On the 45-day transition assistance: happy to provide support, but need to align scope (hours, response SLOs, escalation contact) and whether Redwood can invoice for transition effort or if it comes as a goodwill item.

Laura/Priyom — can you take a look at the attached and suggest a single counterproposal we can give DatumOps? If we can agree on a mutual proposal by EOD Friday (9/4), I will send it back to Samir for confirmation.

Subject: Re: Proposed MSA redlines — notice windows + wind-down

Jordan / Priyom — reviewed DatumOps' v3 redlines. My notes below (high level) — copying Samir so we're transparent about our concerns. I also annotated the PDF and will push a tracked redline if you want these changes in-line.

Legal notes / suggested positions:
- Auto-renew: counter-proposal: keep mechanical auto-renew, but standardize opt-out window to 45 days prior to renewal (compromise between DatumOps' 30d and Redwood's 60d). Alternatively, allow customers to opt-out earlier via the Console (self-serve) with automated confirmation email; contract language should require written confirmation if requested by the customer.
- Termination for convenience: we prefer mutual 60-day termination for convenience. DatumOps' requested 45-day wind-down assistance is reasonable; propose codifying a defined "Transition Assistance" appendix with a capped number of engineering hours (e.g., 80 hours) at standard services rates unless otherwise agreed. This avoids open-ended obligations.
- Credits / refunds: agree to pro-rated credit for prepaid capacity; propose a formula: (unused days / remaining days in billing period) * prepaid amount, subject to minimum 30-day notice for refunds processing.
- Order Form dependence: any SLA or transition assistance must be referenced in the Order Form to avoid implicit operational obligations in the MSA.

Material asks from our side that may be hard stops for DatumOps:
- No indefinite post-termination support without scope/caps or separate SOW.
- Clear data export SLA (48-72 hours for bulk export access) or an agreed schedule in the Order Form.

If Priyom is comfortable with the 45-hour cap recommendation, I will prepare a tracked-counterredline and propose: auto-renew = 45-day opt-out; mutual 60-day termination for convenience; Transition Assistance appendix with 80-hour cap and billing mechanics. If that lands, Jordan can send the counter.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Proposed MSA redlines — notice windows + wind-down

Thanks Laura — appreciate the practical language. DatumOps can accept the mutual 60-day termination for convenience. We are also willing to compromise to a 45-day opt-out window for auto-renew (we had asked for 30).

On transition assistance: we can accept a capped number of hours if Redwood provides a reasonable hourly rate and guarantees response times during the wind-down (we'd like a named escalation contact). Our ask: codify a 45-day minimum wind-down assistance period with deliverables — export access, config snapshot, and two 4-hour knowledge-transfer sessions. If we need to cap hours at 80, we are okay but request a clear exception path if additional work is required for data migration (mutually-agreed SOW).

I attached a short follow-up redline (DatumOps_MSA_Redlines_v4.pdf) with the 45-day opt-out and explicit transition bullets. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept those bullets and the mutual 60-day termination by EOD 10 Sep? If so, I'll prepare the final signatory list and routing for signature.

Attachments: DatumOps_MSA_Redlines_v4.pdf (pdf, 22KB)
